stem: A hospitalized client is being considered for discharge on outpatient parenteral antimicrobial therapy (OPAT). Which care-coordination action is supported by current IDSA OPAT guidance?

options.A: Ensure infectious-diseases expert review occurs before OPAT is initiated.
options.B: Arrange OPAT without specialist review because the route of therapy alone determines whether outpatient treatment is appropriate.
options.C: Assume IV therapy must continue if it was started in the hospital, even when expert review identifies an effective oral alternative.
options.D: Delay all discharge planning until the entire antimicrobial course is completed in the hospital.

rationale: A is correct. The current IDSA OPAT guideline recommends infectious-diseases expert review before initiation of OPAT. The rationale includes antimicrobial stewardship: expert review can identify cases in which parenteral therapy is unnecessary, an oral regimen is appropriate, or antimicrobial therapy itself should be modified. B bypasses the recommended review. C incorrectly treats the inpatient IV route as fixed rather than reassessing whether OPAT is needed. D is incorrect because OPAT is specifically a model for completing appropriate parenteral therapy outside the hospital in selected patients.
educational_objective: Before a client begins OPAT, coordinate infectious-diseases expert review so the indication, antimicrobial choice, route, and outpatient plan are reassessed rather than assuming inpatient IV therapy should automatically continue after discharge.
source_document_title: IDSA 2018 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Outpatient Parenteral Antimicrobial Therapy
source_version_date: Published November 13, 2018; current IDSA OPAT guideline page reviewed 2026-08-17 with no newer replacement guideline identified
source_locator: Antimicrobial Stewardship, Question XVII, Recommendation 17: all patients should have infectious-diseases expert review prior to initiation of OPAT (strong recommendation, very low-quality evidence). Rationale: expert review can curtail unnecessary OPAT and may identify patients for whom oral or no antimicrobial therapy is appropriate; ID review may occur through traditional consultation, an ID care-transition/OPAT stewardship team, or a collaborative pharmacist/ID-physician model.
source_claim_supported: IDSA recommends infectious-diseases expert review before OPAT is initiated, in part to reassess whether parenteral therapy, the selected antimicrobial, and the outpatient plan are appropriate.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, coordinate transitions of care, and assess the need for referrals and resources.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — infectious-diseases review and discharge coordination for OPAT
correction_summary: The raw item used a vague list of reasons for infectious-diseases consultation without an exact current referral standard. It was rebuilt around a specific IDSA recommendation with an exact locator: ID expert review before OPAT initiation. This preserves the collaboration construct while eliminating subjective 'complex infection' referral criteria.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified the IDSA OPAT guideline's explicit Recommendation 17 and checked IDSA's current guideline listings for a newer OPAT replacement; none was identified as of 2026-08-17.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A reproduces the recommendation. B omits required expert review. C ignores the guideline rationale that expert review may avoid unnecessary IV therapy. D incorrectly assumes hospitalization must continue solely because parenteral therapy is prescribed.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; ID expert review should precede OPAT initiation.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; route alone does not establish an appropriate OPAT plan.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; expert review can support oral transition when clinically appropriate.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; appropriate OPAT enables selected clients to complete parenteral therapy outside the hospital.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A states the guideline-supported coordination step. The item does not claim that every complex infection universally requires formal ID consultation outside the OPAT context.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices address discharge and antimicrobial-care coordination.
audit_findings.blueprint: Multidisciplinary collaboration and transition-of-care planning fit Management of Care.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked whether the guideline's 2018 publication date made the item stale. The IDSA page remains the current OPAT guideline and no newer replacement was located. Preserved the stated evidence quality and avoided stronger outcome claims. No second answer remained.
